parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift:39) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift:43) share exactly 3 fields, of which 2 are identical: `makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification` and `name:Notification.Name`. The sole differing slot is the `makeMessage` signature — `AsyncNotificationMessage` takes a plain `Notification` while `MainActorNotificationMessage` takes a `sending Notification`, reflecting their distinct concurrency contexts (async vs. MainActor). Introducing a base protocol `NotificationMessage` in the same `Core` package that carries the two shared members allows each child protocol to retain only its concurrency-specific `makeMessage` variant, eliminating the structural duplication without conflating the two execution contexts. Neither record carries any restraint marker, making this a clean production refactor.
